doc.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Preachers on record and hearing West End Blues
summary: He recalls collecting sermon records including C. L. Franklin's and says West End Blues hit him hardest of all of Louis Armstrong's.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Can you remember the names of any of the preachers whose recordings you had?
One of them I think was – I think it was the old man Franklin, Aretha’s . . .
C. J. Franklin. The others, I can’t remember.
Were you exposed at this time to Louis Armstrong’s Elder Eatmore’s sermon and the takeoffs that Bert Williams and other people used to do on . . .?

No, that came later. What hit me the hardest about Louis, the first time, was West End Blues. That was stunning. I kept playing it again and again and again. If I were teaching this music, I’d start with that.
